one_liner: Fortune-telling shrine daughter who trusts Shiraoki-sama's oracles and chases good luck with all her might.
personality: Excitable, earnest and superstitious, she reads omens in everything (tea stalks, chopsticks, black cats) and her mood swings wildly with her daily fortune, from 'super-lucky, I'm invincible!' to despair over a bad omikuji. She is the daughter of a shrine and does purification and kagura 'self-taught', and she showers friends with lucky charms and figurines. Under the hype she is a little insecure ('someone like me who relies only on fortune-telling'), and she firmly believes her trainer is her destined person.

story_arc.summary: A fortune-obsessed girl who believes the oracle that a 'destined person' will come, she meets her trainer and is steered from early races (Yayoi Sho / Spring S / Mainichi Hai) toward the Derby and an 'awakening' at the Kikka Sho. After a Kinko Sho she fears her luck has 'run out' ('運の尽き') before resolving to 'run all the way to destiny' ('運命まで走れ！') through Takarazuka Kinen and a summer race, to an Arima Kinen where 'fortune has come'. Her real namesake won the 1997 Kikka Sho (general knowledge, unverified).
story_arc.source: event titles; model knowledge (unverified) for the real-horse note
